historical_match.historical_symptom: Two-client process lost one item action per client while Item Graph/player convergence remained otherwise healthy.
historical_match.historical_root_cause: The acceptance worker assigned player.camera_yaw directly. Authoritative look_yaw is derived from player.get_view_basis(), while direct scalar assignment does not rotate the CameraYaw node.
historical_match.historical_fix: m7_playable_network_client_camera_sync_fix.gd used player.adjust_view(...) to synchronize scalar yaw and camera basis before authoritative movement.
historical_match.historical_test_binding: test_m7_playable_networked_processes.gd at e2eda5d spawned the corrected camera-sync worker.

current_subject_regression.conclusion: The current worker again changes only the scalar camera_yaw while both authoritative movement and interaction visibility depend on the actual view/orientation basis. This reintroduces the previously proven Windows acceptance-driver defect.

root_cause: A previously proven test/runtime-driver camera basis synchronization fix was not carried into the current product lineage. Automated M7 steering directly assigns playground.player.camera_yaw instead of using the player's public adjust_view API. The scalar field can therefore diverge from the CameraYaw node/view basis used to derive authoritative orientation_yaw. Movement and item-interaction setup can aim along a stale direction, causing legitimate server spatial/visibility rejection and downstream convergence failure.
